```plato
    //==
    // # IDirectionField2D / IDirectionField3D
    //
    // Fields of unit directions. Evaluation is the generic ValueAt(IField), which
    // already returns the sampled Direction2D / Direction3D, so no interface-
    // specific helper carries weight beyond it.

    //==
    // # IColorField2D / IColorField3D
    //
    // Color fields (procedural textures, gradients, solid textures). Evaluation is
    // the generic ValueAt(IField); no further helper is derivable from Eval alone.

    //==
    // # IComplexField2D
    //
    // A complex-valued planar field. Evaluation is the generic ValueAt(IField);
    // complex-specific analysis needs members Complex does not expose here.

    //==
    // # ITensorField2D / ITensorField3D
    //
    // Matrix-valued fields. Evaluation is the generic ValueAt(IField); tensor
    // invariants are not derivable from the IMatrix surface (see the P3
    // NumericStructures gaps).

    //==
    // # Differentiable field bodies
    //
    // Bodies for the differentiable field interfaces declared in
    // `fields.concepts.plato`: gradient directions, slope, and
    // stationarity for scalar fields, and the divergence / curl classifiers that
    // name local flow behaviour for vector fields.

    //==
    // # IDifferentiableScalarField2D
    //
    // A planar scalar field with an analytic first derivative. The gradient points
    // toward steepest increase; helpers name the directions and critical points.

    // The gradient direction of steepest increase, unit length. Precondition: the
    // gradient is non-zero at the point.
    SteepestAscentDirectionAt(self: IDifferentiableScalarField2D, point: Point2D): Vector2D
        => self.GradientAt(point).Normalize;
```

```plato
    //==
    // # IDifferentiableScalarField3D
    //
    // A spatial scalar field with an analytic first derivative. For a signed
    // distance field the normalized gradient is the outward surface normal.

    // The gradient direction of steepest increase, unit length. Precondition: the
    // gradient is non-zero at the point.
    SteepestAscentDirectionAt(self: IDifferentiableScalarField3D, point: Point3D): Vector3D
        => self.GradientAt(point).Normalize;
```
